verdicts.title: Per-team lifecycle overlay for shared corpus roles: one team's close is not all
verdicts.premise_notes: Central premise holds: jobs.ts:853-855 residual note verbatim; closeRoleIfOpen (684-689), getRoleOpenConfig/setRoleOpenConfig (638-661), listCorpusJobs (917-927), setJobStatus/classifyPublish (167-179/196-201) are all by-id on the shared row; stage-hooks-role-fill.ts:103-108 counts hires per team and closes globally. Minor cites off: close/route.ts canWriteJobLifecycle is at :29 not :31; the role-fill evidence snippet is spread over 103-108 not 106-108; tenancy.ts interview_kits block is 196-207 not 197-204. One grounding gap: getJobWorkspace(id) folds a NULL-owner row into DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID (jobs.ts:825-837), so every public applicant to a corpus role is filed into the DEFAULT team, and the 'team B's in-flight candidates are left on a role B can no longer receive applications for' framing is wrong - the apply doors would read the default team's overlay, never team B's.
verdicts.floor_notes: GATE RULING (coordinator question 1): as written the card changes what a tenant is charged. Today the publish route bills from classifyPublish().billable = !published_at on the SHARED row (publish/route.ts:122-146, job-ingest.ts:201): team B publishing a corpus role team A already took live hits `already: true` and pays nothing. Acceptance case 3 explicitly makes team B's adoption `billable: true` - a new metered job_posts unit per adopting team. That is `irreversible` ('changes what is paid for') and this mode never builds it. It IS revisable to leave billing semantics byte-identical: keep published_at on the shared jobs row and out of the overlay, so classifyPublish keeps the once-per-job-EVER rule. Size L, effort 8, impact 8, risk 7 all inside the floors; write set 9 files + 2 new; honest estimate ~600-800 lines (core.ts migration, seven read folds in jobs.ts with the literal tenant predicate jobs-tenancy.test.ts greps for, three routes, two tests, doc) - at the ceiling. Repo law: new persistent table -> tenancy manifest entry + colocated *-tenancy.test.ts, both in the card.
verdicts.ambition_why: This is the per-tenant move the store's own residual note names, on the same (workspace_id, job_id) shape kits and translations already use - a principal's call, not a tidy-up.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every structural claim stands on the tree; the applicant-filing framing and the billing case misread how the default workspace and published_at actually behave.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Eight store-level cases on the unit DB plus a tenancy source guard would catch a wrong fold or a leaked by-id write; case 3 as written asserts the wrong billing outcome and must be replaced.
verdicts.revise: Drop published_at from the overlay: classifyPublish keeps reading the SHARED jobs.published_at (once-per-job-EVER debit unchanged), and replace acceptance case 3 with: setJobStatus(X, 'published', 'wsA') on a corpus row writes the wsA overlay status AND stamps jobs.published_at as today; classifyPublish(X, 'wsB') afterwards -> { already: false, billable: false }. Also fix the applicant framing: public apply doors resolve the DEFAULT team's overlay (getJobWorkspace folds NULL owners to default), so case 1 should state that closing X in wsA leaves the public apply door open unless wsA is the default team.
